title: Hallucination as a security and business risk

videos.script: A model writes fluent text whether or not it is true. Most of the time that costs a wrong answer. Sometimes it costs much more. {{title}} An airline's chatbot promised a refund the airline's own policy did not offer, and a tribunal made the airline pay. {{tribunal}} Lawyers filed a brief citing cases that did not exist, and a court fined them. {{court}} A model suggests a software package that nobody ever published. Whoever registers that name first decides what the next person installs. {{package}} None of these is a bug you can patch in the model. The defence sits around it. {{defence}} In the lab, every answer has to cite the help centre, the source has to exist, and every number has to appear in it. {{ground}} One answer passes all three and is still wrong, and that is the lesson's honest limit. {{limit}} Then a list of suggested packages meets a snapshot of the registry, and two names are not in it. {{deps}}
